decisions.reason: S-D9 makes the volume control a scroll wheel.
S-D12 says the scroll wheel will be small.
S-D12 says the scroll wheel will be yellow.
S-D2 puts the logo on the front and names the colour scheme but never ties the colour to the logo.
The Advanced Features notes say a docking station will be designed for the remote.
S-D4 and S-D5 describe button placement and level but not button material.
S-D8 states a hard plastic case.
No part says the remote has no LCD screen; S-D10 only mentions a number display.
S-D8 gives a 2D curved shape and S-D11 mostly square with rounded corners.
The notes launch five versions and S-D3 allows different coloured fronts or replacement parts.
The Advanced Features notes and tldr include speech recognition.
S-D7 says the remote will use a regular chip, though the notes say speech recognition requires an advanced one.

action_items.reason: S-A5 has the designers work together on the smart board drawing for the next meeting and S-A7 has the User Interface Designer draw the design.
S-A5 names the Industrial Designer for the prototype drawing on the smart board for the next meeting.
S-A6 has the User Interface Designer settle the button layout options.
